channel.title: Parallax
channel.description: Same event, different vantage points. Geopolitical news compared across Western, Eastern, Middle Eastern and Russian outlets.

item.title: Donald Trump meets with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin during a summit in Shenzhen.
item.description: On November 22, 2026, Donald Trump met with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen to discuss AI regulation, nuclear weapons, and conflicts in Ukraine and the Korean Peninsula. Western outlets focus on the lack of concrete results and frame the interaction as a tactical, skeptical diplomatic exercise. Conversely, Russian state media emphasizes the personal chemistry between the leaders, framing the summit as a successful milestone for global peace and cooperation.

item.title: Iran launches an attack on industrial and military sites in Bahrain involving missile interceptions.
item.description: On November 22, 2026, the Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps launched a missile and drone strike against military and industrial sites in Bahrain, which were partially intercepted by local defenses. While both Eastern and Russian sources confirm the physical exchange, they differ significantly in their framing of the motive. Eastern outlets frame the attack as a response to Western economic pressure and U.S. nuclear policy, whereas Russian sources focus primarily on the immediate military causality and specific hardware.

item.title: Russian cargo ship set on fire by drone attack in the Gulf of Finland
item.description: On November 22, 2026, the Russian cargo vessel *Sparta II* was struck by drones and caught fire while traveling toward Kaliningrad, eventually drifting into Finnish waters. While all outlets confirm the physical reality of the fire and the subsequent Finnish intervention, coverage varies significantly in focus. Western outlets emphasize the tactical implications of the drone strike, whereas Middle Eastern and Eastern sources prioritize the immediate maritime safety risks and the ongoing efforts to contain the fire.

item.title: Negotiations for the COP31 climate agreement face delays over disagreements regarding fossil fuel language.
item.description: Negotiations for the COP31 climate agreement have stalled as delegates debate the specific phrasing regarding fossil fuel phase-outs in the draft agreement. Western outlets focus on the procedural nuances of the text, highlighting the European Union's efforts to balance carbon capture technologies with indirect references to fossil fuel reduction. Conversely, Eastern reporting frames the deadlock as a fundamental conflict between immediate climate goals and the practical realities of global energy sources, emphasizing the absence of explicit commitments to end coal, oil, and gas.
